nodes.description: Experimental, in mouse only. AAV delivery of either CIB2 or CIB3 rescues stereocilia architecture and hearing function in a DFNB48 mouse model. That CIB3 works as well as CIB2 is the therapeutic pay-off of the paralogue-redundancy finding. There is no human trial for DFNB48; the clinical precedent for cochlear gene therapy is OTOF/DFNB9, a different gene.

nodes.description: Mechanotransduction is absent in auditory hair cells of Cib2 mutant mice, and MET currents are abolished in Cib2-deficient outer hair cells. The result that carries the mechanistic weight is the qualifier: this happens despite the presence of tip links. Tip links are the filaments that transmit force to the channel, so their being intact localises the lesion to the channel complex rather than to the force-delivery apparatus.

nodes.description: Biallelic CIB2 variants abolish or impair the protein. The most prevalent allele in the original human families is the missense p.Phe91Ser, which was modelled directly as a knock-in mouse. Variants act regionally rather than uniformly: those in the N-terminal region disrupt the TMC1/TMC2 interaction without affecting calcium buffering, C-terminal variants affect only calcium buffering, and middle-region variants do both.

nodes.description: Constitutive Cib2 null. Deaf, with mechanotransduction absent in auditory hair cells while tip links remain present, and with overgrowth of the shorter transducing stereocilia rows. Vestibular function is spared, matching the human non-syndromic phenotype.

Carries the single most prevalent human DFNB48 allele rather than a null, so it tests whether the disease missense variant, and not merely absence of the protein, causes the phenotype. It does: these mice are deaf with the same transduction and bundle defects.

Standard management for severe-to-profound prelingual sensorineural hearing loss. It bypasses the failed hair-cell transduction step by stimulating the cochlear nerve directly, so it addresses the consequence of the lesion rather than the lesion itself.

nodes.description: CIB2 binds TMC1 and TMC2 through a conserved hydrophobic groove, engaging a domain of TMC1/2 flanked by transmembrane domains 2 and 3. The architecture mirrors KChIP auxiliary subunits binding Kv4 channels, which is the structural argument for calling CIB2 an auxiliary subunit. Deafness-causing CIB2 mutations disrupt this interaction and perturb TMC1/2 localisation and function.

nodes.description:
Beyond its channel role, CIB2 limits the length of the shorter, transducing rows of stereocilia: these overgrow in the hair bundles of Cib2 mutants, degrading the graded "staircase" architecture the bundle needs. This is a structural arm distinct from the channel arm.
CIB2 does bind whirlin (WHRN) - the EF2 domain of CIB2 to the HHD2 region of WHRN - but the stereocilia role is not exercised *through* whirlin, which is the natural assumption and is wrong. Cib2/Whrn double homozygous mutants show the bundle phenotype of the Whrn single mutant rather than an additive one, overexpressing WHRN does not rescue Cib2-null stereocilia, and double heterozygotes hear normally, so there is no digenic interaction. What does change in Cib2-null hair cells is MYO15A, which over-accumulates at the tips of the first-row stereocilia. Whirlin itself, along with myosin XVa, Eps8 and Eps8L2, still reaches the stereocilia tips in Cib2 mutants, so CIB2 is not required to deliver them.
The positive mechanism is not settled, and three candidates have been raised across this literature. PMID:28663585 offers two in its discussion: that CIB2 is part of the myosin XVa/whirlin elongation complex, and that it buffers free calcium near the MET channels at the stereocilia tips, where a local calcium change would alter actin remodelling. PMID:40083274 offers a third, that CIB2 acts in the GPSM2-GNAI elongation complex.
Two of the three are disfavoured on evidence this entry already carries, and are recorded here as retired rather than dropped. The myosin XVa/whirlin route is what the WHRN independence results above argue against. The calcium-buffering route is undercut by PMID:26173970: the p.F91S and p.R66W deafness substitutions do not alter the calcium buffering ability of CIB2, so a buffering deficit cannot be the mechanism by which those alleles cause disease. Neither is refuted outright - the buffering result covers two alleles, and p.I123T and p.R186W are reported to impair buffering - so the retirement is on the balance of the evidence, not a disproof.
That leaves GPSM2-GNAI as the live candidate, and it is worth being precise about what it would and would not mean. It is not a whirlin route reintroduced under another name, but neither is it a claim that WHRN is uninvolved in elongation: GPSM2-GNAI itself binds WHRN and is carried to the stereocilia tips by MYO15A. The open question is which complex CIB2 acts in, not whether WHRN participates at all. The authors put it no higher than speculation and this entry does not adopt it as a mechanism arm.
The same paper separates this arm from the channel arm on the phenotype itself: rows 2 and 3 elongate in Cib2 mutants, whereas loss of mechanotransduction current makes transducing stereocilia retract. The overgrowth therefore cannot simply be downstream of the channel defect, which is the reason this node sits parallel to the transduction node rather than beneath it.

nodes.description: Loss of transduction and disorganised bundle architecture together produce hair-cell dysfunction and, subsequently, hair-cell death. Because cochlear hair cells are not replaced in mammals, this is the step that makes the deafness permanent and sets the therapeutic window for any gene-replacement approach.
